details: Bitcoin's price slipped below $75,000 as crypto markets failed to mirror a rebound in technology stocks, following stronger-than-expected US payrolls data. This market reaction, coupled with over $1 billion in liquidations across crypto markets, indicates a risk-off sentiment. Persistent outflows from US-listed Bitcoin spot ETFs are also contributing to the downward pressure, with Bitcoin potentially heading for its fifth consecutive weekly loss.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $75K as Crypto Markets Miss Tech Stock Rebound Amid US Jobs Data

details: The US Treasury Department has withdrawn its controversial "travel rule" proposal, which would have required crypto firms to collect and transmit more data on transactions. This move is seen as a significant relief for the crypto industry, potentially easing compliance burdens and fostering innovation within the sector.
title: US Treasury Walks Back Crypto Surveillance 'Travel Rule' Proposal

details: The Trump administration is advancing plans to allow cryptocurrencies in 401(k) retirement accounts, with the proposal now reaching the White House for final review. This regulatory development could significantly broaden access to crypto investments for mainstream investors and potentially unlock a new wave of capital into the digital asset space.
title: Trump Administration Moves Closer to Allowing Crypto in 401(k) Retirement Plans

details: Nigeria's central bank has unveiled new regulations for stablecoins, requiring licensing for issuers while explicitly banning algorithmic stablecoins. This move aims to provide regulatory clarity and consumer protection within the rapidly growing Nigerian crypto market, focusing on asset-backed stablecoins.
title: Nigeria Introduces Stablecoin Licensing Rules, Bans Algorithmic Versions

details: Crypto card provider Gnosis Pay announced a data breach that exposed customer information, although customer funds remain unaffected. The company detected unauthorized access and has since replaced compromised security credentials and fixed the vulnerability. This incident highlights ongoing security challenges in the crypto ecosystem.
title: Gnosis Pay Data Breach Exposes Customer Info, Funds Unaffected

details: Russia has approved new rules allowing retail investors to trade major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, through regulated intermediaries. This development opens legal access to crypto markets for millions of Russian citizens, potentially driving new demand and increasing adoption in the region.
title: Russia Approves Retail Bitcoin Trading

details: BitMine (formerly MicroStrategy) continues its accumulation of Ethereum, adding another 5,000 ETH and bringing its total holdings to approximately 6.065 million ETH, representing 4.96% of the total supply. This sustained accumulation by a major institutional player signals strong conviction in Ethereum's long-term value.
title: BitMine Buys More Ethereum, Accumulating 4.96% of Total Supply

details: Circle, the issuer of USDC stablecoin, has minted 250 million USDC on the Solana blockchain. This significant minting activity on Solana indicates growing utilization and liquidity for the network, highlighting its increasing role in the stablecoin ecosystem and potentially driving further adoption.
title: Circle Mints 250 Million USDC on Solana, Boosting Network Activity

details: Stacks (STX) saw a 4.5% price surge following the successful sale of its third Bitcoin staking bond, which attracted 1,005 BTC and significant interest from high-profile institutions. This indicates growing institutional confidence in Bitcoin staking solutions built on the Stacks layer.
title: Stacks (STX) Surges on Institutional Bitcoin Staking Bond Sale

details: Zcash (ZEC) experienced a 3% price increase following its NU7 upgrade, which introduced faster blocks and a supply shock to the network. This positive price action for Zcash stands in contrast to a generally flat broader crypto market, driven by project-specific fundamental improvements.
title: Zcash (ZEC) Surges on NU7 Upgrade Amidst Flat Crypto Market
